title: Outdoor STEM Challenge Cards
goal: 24 hands-on building and problem-solving challenges you do outside with sticks, rocks, leaves and whatever else is lying around. Your kid plans, builds, tests and improves, just like a real engineer: a shelter that blocks the wind, a bridge that holds five stones, a raft that carries pebbles. No kits, just a few kitchen extras, and the first design is supposed to fail.
need: These cards, on your phone or printed and cut out
Fallen natural materials: sticks, rocks, leaves, pinecones, sand
Optional: a phone for 'design photos' of each version
For some cards: a raw egg, a cup, a watering can (or a second cup), and a plastic bottle (you cut it)

lesson.text: Every challenge runs on the same engineering loop: plan it, build it, test it, improve it. The improving is where the real learning happens, so the first try failing is part of the plan.
lesson.before: It fell down. It doesn't work.

model.line: Two long sticks across the gap, with small sticks laid across them like a deck.
Built it in five minutes between two rocks.
It held 2 stones, then sagged in the middle.
Added a flat rock under the middle as a support. Now it holds 5.

lesson.modelNote: 'It doesn't work' became 'it sagged in the middle', and that one detail showed exactly where the support rock had to go.

academics.subject: Science
academics.text: forces, materials, water flow, insulation and sound

academics.subject: Engineering
academics.text: the design loop: plan, build, test, improve

academics.subject: Math
academics.text: measuring height, counting loads, comparing designs, and timing tests

academics.subject: Life skills
academics.text: persistence, learning from failure, and respecting nature

howTo.intro: Resist building it for them when the first version collapses. Be the test instead: blow on the shelter, add stones to the bridge, and get more excited about version 2 than version 1. Use only fallen materials, never break living plants, and take builds apart when you're done.

plan.what: Pick 3 to 5 cards, or let your kid choose.
Plan, build, test, improve. About 15 to 30 minutes each.
Take a photo of the best design, then take it apart and leave the space as you found it.

troubleshoot.q: They get frustrated when it falls apart
troubleshoot.a: Say it out loud: engineers expect the first version to fail. Then ask about one thing to change, not everything.
Use a puddle, a dish of water or a dry channel. Never block a real stream, and stay close near water.

skills.name: Persistence
skills.text: improving after the first try fails

skills.name: Materials sense
skills.text: knowing what's strong, flexible, waterproof or warm

levelsLine: Three levels on every card. Explore: do the challenge. Develop: add the Deeper part. Extend: build two versions, test both, and explain which worked better and why.

cards.name: Windproof Shelter
cards.t: Build a mini shelter that blocks wind, using only fallen sticks, leaves and rocks.
cards.d: Test it by gently blowing or fanning, then improve it twice.

cards.name: Bridge Builder
cards.t: Build a bridge that spans a small gap between two rocks or logs.
cards.d: Make it hold 5 small stones without collapsing.

cards.name: Tallest Tower
cards.t: Build the tallest free-standing tower you can using found items.
cards.d: It must survive a gentle 'wind test' for 5 seconds.

cards.name: Ground Anchor
cards.t: Push a stick into the ground, tie on a string and pull. When does it pop out?
cards.d: Lean the stick away from the pull, like a tent peg. Does it hold more?

cards.name: Egg Nest
cards.t: Build a nest from leaves, grass and sticks that keeps a raw egg safe when it's dropped from knee height. Wash hands after.
cards.d: Raise the drop to waist height. What did you have to change?

cards.name: Water Wheel
cards.t: Build a little wheel from sticks and leaves that spins when you pour water over it.
cards.d: Change the paddles: bigger, smaller or more of them. Which spins fastest?

cards.name: Raft Challenge
cards.t: Build a tiny raft that can carry 3 pebbles on water.
cards.d: Redesign it to carry 5 pebbles.

cards.name: Erosion Barrier
cards.t: Make a small barrier that would slow down water flowing down a slope.
cards.d: Build two versions and decide which works better, and why.

cards.name: Mini Dam
cards.t: Build a mini dam across a dry channel or between rocks. Never block a real stream.
cards.d: Pour a cup of water at the top of the channel. Where does it go around your dam, and how do you stop it?

cards.name: Rain Catcher
cards.t: Design a collector from leaves or bark that catches the most 'rain' from a watering can.
cards.d: Measure each design's catch in a cup. Which shape wins?

cards.name: Beam Test
cards.t: Lay a stick across two stones and hang a bag of pebbles from its middle. How far does it sag?
cards.d: Tie two thin sticks together. Do they beat one thick stick?

cards.name: The Waterproof Test
cards.t: Find 3 natural surfaces that look waterproof and 3 that look absorbent.
cards.d: Drip water on each and count the seconds until it soaks in or rolls off. Was your guess right?

cards.name: The Best Insulator
cards.t: Bury your hand for a minute in 3 piles: leaf litter, pine needles, dry grass. Check each pile first for anything sharp or crawling. Which feels warmest on a cool day?
cards.d: Fluff one pile, pack one hard. Which is warmer? (Trapped air.)

cards.name: Mud Brick
cards.t: Shape two mud bricks, one with dry grass mixed in. Leave both in the sun until tomorrow.
cards.d: Which one cracked? Drop both from knee height to test strength.

cards.name: Muddy Water Filter
cards.t: Layer sand, gravel and leaves in a bottle your grown-up cuts, to make muddy water clearer. Never drink it.
cards.d: Change the order of the layers. Does the water come out clearer?

cards.name: Marble Run, No Marbles
cards.t: Build a track with sticks, rocks and leaves that guides a round object (an acorn, a seed, a pebble) downhill.
cards.d: Add a turn, and keep it from falling off.

cards.name: Bark Sled
cards.t: Make a sled from fallen bark or a flat stick that slides farthest down a slope.
cards.d: Change only the bottom: smooth bark, rough bark, a leaf underneath. Which wins?

cards.name: Friction Test
cards.t: Put a stone, a pinecone and a leaf on a flat piece of bark. Tilt it slowly. Which slides first?
cards.d: Wet the bark or add sand. What changes?

cards.name: Pendulum Count
cards.t: Hang a stone on a string from a branch. Count its swings in 10 seconds.
cards.d: Shorten the string, then try a heavier stone. Which changes the count?

cards.name: Balance Mobile
cards.t: Hang 3 found objects from one stick so it hangs level.
cards.d: Add a fourth without taking anything off. Where does it have to go?

cards.name: Pinecone Weather Station
cards.t: Put one pinecone in a cup of water and one in the sun. Check both after 2 hours.
cards.d: Keep a dry one by the door. Does it close up before rain?

cards.name: Leaf Megaphone
cards.t: Roll a big leaf or a strip of bark into a cone and call to someone 20 steps away.
cards.d: Make it longer or wider. Which carries your voice farther?

cards.name: Leaf Roof
cards.t: Build a roof that keeps a dry leaf dry under a cup of 'rain'.
cards.d: Say it out loud: 'My first roof leaked because... I fixed it by...'

cards.name: Shadow Clock
cards.t: Push a stick into the ground and mark the shadow tip now, then again each time you finish another card.
cards.d: Predict where the shadow will be in an hour, then check.

conclusion.headline: Version 2 held more, and they knew why.
conclusion.text: The next block tower or blanket fort that collapses will tell you. If they look for the exact spot it gave way before rebuilding, the loop from these cards has stuck. If they start over from scratch, ask where it broke first.
conclusion.celebrate: The moment the second bridge beats the first, put a finger on the support they added and say: 'This rock is why it held five. You found that.'
extensions: Build a full-size lean-to with a grown-up, using the Windproof Shelter rules
Look up how beavers build dams, and compare with your Mini Dam
Give a younger kid one card and be their tester: blow, pour, add stones
Pick one card and write the 'failure log': every version, what broke, what you changed

signs: They expect the first try to fail and keep going
They change one thing at a time and test again
They explain why a design worked, not just that it did
makeItReal: Give everyone the same card and 15 minutes, grown-ups too. Then test every design together, one at a time, and let whoever built the strongest one explain to the rest of you what made it hold.
cta: Want the next one? This guide is one of 120+ in the Anywhere Learning library, each with your job and your kid's job at every step.

photo.caption: Card 1, full size: my son's shelter in the woods near our house.

fromHome.text: My son and a friend spent an afternoon in the woods in our neighbourhood building a shelter like this one, from nothing but fallen sticks leaned against a tree. Nobody gave them instructions: they figured out the angles, the support and what kept it standing by trying, failing and fixing it.

classroom.intro: Engineering challenges work well with a class: groups plan, build, test and improve with fallen materials, and every group's first version is supposed to fail. You play the test, not the builder.

tips.d: Jobs: a planner who sketches the design, two builders, and a tester who runs the test and records the result. Rotate jobs between version 1 and version 2.
Give every group the same card on the same day, like Bridge Builder or Raft Challenge. It turns the final test into a fair comparison across the whole class.
Gather fallen sticks, rocks and leaves into a pile for each group. For water cards, bring one bin of water and cups to share. You cut any plastic bottles beforehand.
Run the tests yourself or with a rotating student tester: blow on each shelter, add stones to each bridge. Cheer for version 2 louder than version 1.
Egg Nest drops happen outside, with hand washing after. Mini Dam stays in a dry channel or sand tray, never a real stream. Nobody drinks the Muddy Water Filter water, and check insulator piles first.
Each group photographs every version on a class tablet. End with a two-minute share: what failed, what changed, and why version 2 worked better. Then take builds apart and leave the space clean.

classroom.timing: Each card takes 15 to 30 minutes, so a 45-minute period fits one card with the share and clean-up. Run one card a week; Mud Brick and Pinecone Weather Station need a later check, and favourite cards go home to try.
